lesson: Class — 30 Aug: looking for a flat
grammar: أَرَادَ أَنْ + present (wanted to…), يُمْكِنُكَ + verbal noun (you can…), and the feminine agreement that runs right through the description of the flat

sentences.ar: فِي يَوْمِ الأَحَدِ، أَرَادَ سَامِر أَنْ يَبْحَثَ عَنْ بَيْتٍ جَدِيدٍ لِلسَّكَنِ.
sentences.en: On Sunday, Samer wanted to look for a new house to live in.

sentences.ar: ذَهَبَ مَعَ أَخِيهِ إِلَى حَيِّ الجَامِعَةِ، وَشَاهَدَا شَقَّةً جَمِيلَةً فِيهَا غُرْفَةُ جُلُوسٍ وَاسِعَةٌ وَغُرْفَةُ نَوْمٍ مُرِيحَةٌ وَمَطْبَخٌ صَغِيرٌ.
sentences.en: He went with his brother to the university neighbourhood, and the two of them saw a beautiful flat with a spacious living room, a comfortable bedroom and a small kitchen.
words: and the two of them saw

sentences.ar: كَانَ فِي غُرْفَةِ النَّوْمِ سَرِيرٌ وَمِرْآةٌ، وَفِي المَطْبَخِ فُرْنٌ جَدِيدٌ.
sentences.en: In the bedroom there was a bed and a mirror, and in the kitchen a new oven.

sentences.ar: سَأَلَ سَامِر صَاحِبَ البَيْتِ: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، هَلْ هَذِهِ الشَّقَّةُ مُتَاحَةٌ يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ؟
sentences.en: Samer asked the owner of the house: please, is this flat available on Tuesday?

sentences.ar: فَأَجَابَهُ: نَعَمْ، يُمْكِنُكَ الدُّخُولُ يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ، وَإِذَا أَرَدْتَ يُمْكِنُكَ الانْتِقَالُ يَوْمَ الخَمِيسِ.
sentences.en: So he answered him: yes, you can move in on Tuesday, and if you want you can move on Thursday.

sentences.ar: أَعْجَبَتْ سَامِر الشَّقَّةُ، فَقَالَ: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَسْكُنَ هُنَا، فَالبَيْتُ جَمِيلٌ وَالحَيُّ هَادِئٌ.
sentences.en: The flat pleased Samer, so he said: I want to live here — the house is beautiful and the neighbourhood is quiet.

vocab.note: from شَقَّ — to split; a flat is a 'split off' part of a building
same root as حَيّ 'alive' — أَسْكُنُ فِي حَيِّ المَطَارِ
root س‑ك‑ن — to settle, dwell; also سَكِينَة 'tranquillity'
instrument-noun from رَأَى — to see; the thing you see with
الوَاسِع is also a name of Allah — the All-Encompassing
verbal noun of دَخَلَ — to enter
verbal noun of انْتَقَلَ — to move from place to place
Arabic says 'the flat pleased Samer', not 'Samer liked the flat'

vocab.en: you can, it is possible for you
vocab.note: followed by a verbal noun: يُمْكِنُكَ الدُّخُولُ

translate.en: Is this flat available on Tuesday?
translate.ar: هَلْ هَذِهِ الشَّقَّةُ مُتَاحَةٌ يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ؟

translate.en: In the kitchen there is a new oven.
